newsitem.title: USA: Ohio blind man struck by truck hit for jaywalking.
newsitem.headline: Ohio blind man struck by truck hit for jaywalking.

text.p: A blind man ticketed for jaywalking after he was hit by a pickup truck will contest the charge because an Ohio law gives the sightless right of way, his lawyer said on Wednesday.

Jeff Friedlander, 48, said he was hit as he tried to cross the street in the rain on Jan. 22 and suffered a broken tailbone. Then officer Chauncey Prude charged him with walking outside the crosswalk and against a red light.

"I was shocked and I didn't deserve the ticket ... I guess he didn't give a hoot whether I was blind or sighted," the Cincinnati Enquirer quoted Friedlander as saying. He pleaded not guilty in Hamilton County traffic court on Tuesday and was told to return on March 5 for trial.
His attorney, Douglas May, told Reuters on Wednesday that a blind pedestrian with a white cane has right of way over any motor vehicle under Ohio law.

But local prosecutor Charles Rubenstein said Friedlander forfeited his right of way when he ventured outside the crosswalk and against the light. He said his office would decide whether to prosecute the case, which could result in a $46 fine plus court costs, after consulting with Prude.
